channel.title: Comments on: Best Brainstorming Tool: Instant Messaging
channel.description: Instant Usability & Web Standards — static archive

item.title: By: Dan
item.dc:creator: Dan
item.description: The other day I ran across a nifty and neat brainstorming utility and free of charge I might add. It works based on the thought from permutating diverse components from your concept into a list and then the website permutates fresh arrangements based on the list, which in turn propogates aspects you would never think of. After running across it, I use it a great deal, because it does help conceptually amazingly good. Free Brainstorming Software

item.title: By: Claus
item.dc:creator: Claus
item.description: Totally buying it – it’s not even coworker dependent. Chances are coworkers you don’t click with on IM won’t click with you over email. In that case – whiteboards and handwaving is the only option.

item.title: By: Thomas Baekdal
item.dc:creator: Thomas Baekdal
item.description:
Sound about right, I have had a few IM brainstorming sessions – and all of them was more productive than other forms (including for me – face-to-face brainstorming meetings).

I think the key is the speed of interaction, and feedback – with the ability to be alone to think.

One thing missing for me is a good visualization. Sure you can send images via IM, but you cannot sketch something out as you present the idea.
